role: The code map's call graph: parses every Swift file with tree-sitter for calls, property reads, bare references, conformances and closure assignments; resolves each to unit keys as certain or possible edges; adds recorded calls, protocol-requirement dispatch and Makefile/workflow/script wiring. `build` is the from-scratch definition; index.py keeps the same graph up to date incrementally from the same parts (unit_table, recorded_edges, swift_file, Resolver, wiring_edges, assemble). Imported by index.py and codemap.py.
state: COMMON: member names (count, map, load, save, start, reset, ...) so common in Swift/Foundation/SwiftUI that a unique repo match on an unknown receiver is only a possible edge
NOT_A_REFERENCE: syntax-node parent types under which a simple_identifier is a declaration, label, type or member name rather than a reference
FUNC_KINDS / PROP_KINDS: inventory unit kinds that can be called / read as properties
toplevel: Module docstring defining certain and possible edges, `from __future__ import annotations`, imports (collections, re, Path, NS_CODE from inventory), the three constants above, TEST_TARGETS (EmuquTests/, EmuquUITests/), is_test_file, _PARSER (the lazily made Swift parser) and the Resolver class statement. tree_sitter is imported inside swift_file.

units.does: Parses one Swift file and walks it once, returning four things: refs (unit start line -> list of (kind 'call'|'prop', name, argument labels, trailing-closure count, (receiver kind, receiver type))), params (function/init/subscript start line -> [(external label, has default)]), conforms (type or protocol name -> names in its inheritance clause; extensions included, generic arguments and module prefixes stripped) and closure_assigns (stored-property name -> start lines of units that assign a closure literal to it). References in code outside every unit (Swift top-level code) are not collected.
Source text of a node: the raw bytes in its byte range, decoded with replacement.
For a call_expression, returns the label of each value argument in its call_suffix ('_' when unlabeled) and the number of trailing closures.

branches.cond: child is not the call suffix

units.does: Classifies what a member reference is made on: no target -> ('implicit', None); self or Self -> ('self', None); super -> ('super', None); a call whose callee is a capitalised identifier (a constructor, `Foo(...)`) -> ('type', 'Foo'); a capitalised dotted name -> ('type', its last component); anything else (a variable, a chain) -> ('unknown', None).

branches.cond: constructor call of a capitalised name

units.does: Recursive walk carrying the start line of the innermost enclosing unit. A class/struct/enum/extension/protocol declaration adds its inheritance clause to conforms. A function/init/deinit/subscript/protocol-function/property declaration that starts on a unit's start line becomes the current unit; for non-properties its parameters (external name, else name, else '_'; with whether a default follows) go to params. Inside a unit: a call on a bare identifier is an implicit-receiver call; a call on a navigation expression is a call with its receiver classified; a call on `.name` (implicit member) is a call with unknown receiver; prefix operators (`!f()`, `-f()`) are unwrapped to their operand first. A navigation expression that is not itself a callee is a property read with its receiver. A bare identifier not under a NOT_A_REFERENCE parent and not a callee is an implicit-receiver property read. An assignment whose right side is a closure literal records the target's last identifier in closure_assigns.

branches.effect: its inheritance specifiers added to conforms[name]

branches.cond: declaration node on a unit's start line
a default value follows a parameter

units.does: Builds the whole graph from scratch: the unit table, every record's recorded calls, swift_file for every Swift file in the inventory, each file's references resolved by one Resolver, its protocol-requirement edges and the build wiring, assembled into {'edges': {src: {dst: kind}}, 'units': ..., 'why': {(src, dst): reasons}}. The commands read the same graph from index.py; index.py --verify compares the two.
{node: inventory entry plus its file} for every unit, and a `path::` node of kind 'file' (name the path, lines 1 to the file's length) for every file.

The graph from (src, dst, kind, reason) contributions in any order: a contribution from or to a node not in `units`, or from a node to itself, is dropped; an edge is certain when any contribution is (never downgraded to possible); a certain edge keeps every reason given with a certain contribution, sorted.

branches.cond: src or dst unknown, or src == dst

units.does: A certain contribution, reason 'recorded', from each unit record to every `path::key` its `calls` names (not ext:/dyn:/closure: entries). The source unit's existence is checked later, by assemble.
One Swift file's _swift_refs output (references, parameter lists, conformances, closure assignments) with unit start lines turned into node keys; the tree-sitter parser is made once, on first use.
The last dotted part of a type name ('' for None).

Merges every Swift file's parameter lists, conformances and closure assignments, indexes units by name (Swift units and C/Objective-C functions), and takes the repository's types: every unit's short type name and every type that declares a conformance.
A type's short name with every ancestor and protocol it conforms to, transitively.
Whether a unit is a function or initializer with a parameter that has no default value.

The units named `name` that a reference of `kind` can mean: a call matches functions whose labels bind (_labels_match) and properties; a property reference matches properties and functions; optionally only global ones, or only those whose short type is in `types`.
(src, dst, kind, reason) for every reference of every unit of one file (resolve).

The edges one unit's references resolve to. A bare call of a repository type name goes to that type's label-matching initializers (certain if one, reason 'initializer'). A reference on self, super or an implicit receiver resolves within the unit's own type family ('own type'); an implicit one with no match falls back to same-file units ('same file'), then global functions ('global function'). A receiver typed by a repository type resolves within that type's family ('typed receiver'); any other receiver against every unit of that name ('unique name'). One candidate gives a certain edge unless the receiver was unresolved and the name is COMMON; then filters drop candidates the reference cannot mean (a property read on an unresolved receiver drops functions that need arguments; app code drops test-target units). An implicit property reference with no candidate is ignored; a call with none whose name is an assigned stored closure gives possible edges to the assigning units ('stored closure').

units.does: A certain edge, reason 'protocol requirement', from each protocol requirement to each same-named, label-compatible function (not itself a requirement) of the protocol or a type that conforms to it.

Certain contributions, reason 'build wiring', among scripts, Makefile targets and workflow jobs and steps: a target to its prerequisites; target recipes, jobs and steps to each `make`/`$(MAKE)` target and each scripts/ or Tools/ .sh/.py path (file node) they name; a job to its steps; Python and shell functions to the local functions (and, for Python, top-level defs imported from sibling modules) named in their body; a script's code outside units to its functions and the scripts it names.
